errors.why: The side simply ends mid-verse with 'likewise' and the text continues on the next side; 'text breaks off' is an unmarked editorial insertion that misrepresents the source.

note: Faithful rendering of the Buddha's verses to his questioners (no teacher, self-awakened, going to Vārāṇasī) with only minor glossing liberties.
Accurate and readable rendering of the pregnant doe's plea to Devadatta and the Bodhisattva; the clumsy bracketed gloss on mṛga is harmless.

errors.english: Even if there is a gathering [note: an assembly of conditions], because
errors.why: In this refutation of the Nyāya self, 'du ba is samavāya, the inherence of cognition in the self, not a gathering of conditions; the note is wrong.

fix.find: Even if there is a gathering [note: an assembly of conditions], because
fix.replace: Even though there is inherence (samavāya), because

errors.english: in the case where memory and experience are distinct
errors.why: It is the self, which is distinct from memory and experience, that is shown not to be a rememberer etc.; memory and experience are not said to be distinct from each other.

errors.english: Because if that were the case, it would change.
errors.why: The root phrase states positive concomitance: memory occurs when that (experience/vāsanā) occurs; 'gyur here means 'arise/occur', not 'change'.

note: The commentary's thread is broadly followed, but the inherence term and several root-text lemmata are misread, so the argument against the Nyāya self is blurred.

errors.english: The existence of a yellow that is an object of perception depends on non-perception.
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of a yellow that is NOT an object of perception; the negation is lost.

fix.find: The existence of a yellow that is an object of perception depends on non-perception.
fix.replace: The existence of a yellow that is not an object of perception depends on non-perception.

errors.english: there is a discerning of yellow and other colors
errors.why: rnam par gcod pa is exclusion (vyavaccheda): the cognition of blue, like its own nature, excludes yellow etc., not 'discerns' them.

errors.english: Otherwise, pleasure might exist but not appear
errors.why: gzhan here is 'another person': another's pleasure exists but does not appear (to me), not 'otherwise'.

errors.english: Establishing things in their proper order is the temporary state.
errors.why: gnas skabs here means the proper occasion/relevance (as with gnas skabs ma yin pa 'out of place' earlier), not a 'temporary state'.

note: A dense Pramāṇa commentary on non-perception whose logic the English repeatedly loses (negation dropped, exclusion and occasion misrendered, bdag med pa read as selflessness), so it needs a specialist's pass.
The Tibetan verses of this bilingual side (Anaṅgaṇa, Vipaśyin, the contest of offerings with King Bandhumat) are rendered faithfully, with the Sanskrit used sensibly for names.

errors.english: This is because one intends to establish the (sadhya) the thesis or what is to be proven solely through the very similarity with the example itself.
errors.why: sgrub par byed pa is the probans (sādhana): the similarity with the example is itself held to be the means of proof, which is why there is no difference to warrant the ablative.

fix.find: This is because one intends to establish the (sadhya) the thesis or what is to be proven solely through the very similarity with the example itself.
fix.replace: This is because the very similarity with the example itself is intended to be the means of proof (sādhana).

note: The grammatical argument about the ablative and apposition is well followed, except for the key sādhya/sādhana confusion at its centre.
Accurate rendering of the Daśabhūmika citation and of the argument that ignorance is an inverted cognition rather than merely associated with view.

errors.english: because contradictory things cannot possibly be a single valid cognition
errors.why: The point is that contradictory properties cannot both be validly cognized in one locus, not that they cannot be a single valid cognition.

note: Sound rendering of the discussion of the refuted thesis and the fourfold division of invalidation, with one muddled clause.

errors.english: how could the awareness of past things and the like be direct perception
errors.why: The sentence (completed on the next side with a 'because' clause) explains how knowing the past is perception; the rhetorical 'how could' implies the opposite.

note: Faithful rendering of the argument on yogic perception and sense activity; only the side-final question is framed as a denial.
Faithful and elegant rendering of the spring forest, the verses, and the king's scheme to test the ascetic's power.
